create_folder.description: Create a folder to keep pastes in, at the top level or inside one of your folders.

parameters.name: parent_folder

create_multi_file_paste.description: Share several named files as one paste, each highlighted for its own language, such as a script with its log or config.
create_multi_file_paste.name: create_multi_file_paste

parameters.description: Each file's name and contents, such as app.py and its code. The name's ending sets how Pastefy highlights that file. A files list an earlier step returned works too.
parameters.name: files

parameters.description: Optional. The paste's name, which works like a file name: end it in .py, .md, .json and so on, and Pastefy highlights the paste in that language.
parameters.name: title

parameters.description: Who can open the paste.
parameters.name: visibility

options.label: Unlisted: anyone with the link can open it
Public: also listed on Pastefy's Explore page and your profile
Private: only your Pastefy account can open it

parameters.description: Optional. One of your folders to put the paste in. Leave blank to keep it at the top level.
parameters.name: folder

parameters.description: Optional. Words to file the paste under, such as python or notes, each up to 30 characters.
parameters.name: tags

parameters.description: How long the paste lasts before Pastefy deletes it for good, counted from when this step runs.
parameters.name: delete_after

parameters.description: Encrypt the paste in Lodol before it is sent, so Pastefy only ever stores scrambled text. Lodol makes up a password unless you give one, and returns it with a secret link that opens the paste.
parameters.name: encrypt

parameters.description: Optional. A password to encrypt the paste with; giving one turns on Encrypt. Anyone opening the paste on Pastefy will need it.
parameters.name: password

content.description: The paste's text. A multi-file paste keeps its files here as JSON; use files instead.

multi_file.description: True for a paste of several named files.

owner.description: The Pastefy user name of the paste's owner.

password.description: The password the paste was encrypted with, given or made up. Empty when it isn't encrypted.

raw_url.description: A link to the paste's bare text, with no page around it.

secret_link.description: For an encrypted paste: its link with the password built in, which opens it straight away. Empty otherwise, or when the password has spaces or other characters a link can't carry.

status.description: Status of the action execution ("success" on success).

url.description: The paste's link, to open or share.

update_paste.description: Change a paste's title, text or files, who can open it, its folder, tags or when it is deleted. Blank fields stay as they are.

parameters.description: The paste: pick one of yours, or give a paste's ID or link, such as the url an earlier step returned. An encrypted paste's secret link opens it without a password.
parameters.name: paste

parameters.description: Optional. A new title, which works like a file name: its ending sets the highlighting.
parameters.name: title

parameters.description: Optional. New text to replace the paste's text with. A multi-file paste becomes a single-file one.
parameters.name: content

parameters.description: Optional. Files to replace the paste's text or files with, each a name and its contents. Give these or Content, not both.
parameters.name: files

parameters.description: Optional. Who can open the paste from now on.
parameters.name: visibility

options.label: Unlisted: anyone with the link can open it
Public: also listed on Pastefy's Explore page and your profile
Private: only your Pastefy account can open it

parameters.name: folder

parameters.description: Optional. Tags to replace the paste's tags with. Leave empty to keep them.
parameters.name: tags

parameters.description: Optional. A new time for Pastefy to delete the paste, counted from when this step runs. Pastefy can move an expiry but not remove it.
parameters.name: delete_after

parameters.description: Only for an encrypted paste: its password, which changing its title, text or files needs. Not needed when Paste is its secret link.
